skill.name: golang-concurrency
skill.description: Guides concurrent Go implementation and review through goroutine lifecycle management, channel ownership, synchronization, bounded workers, and cancellation.
skill.summary: Design and review concurrent Go code with structured lifecycle, synchronization, and pipeline guidance.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 66 static alerts are false positives involving formatting, illustrative Go identifiers, documentation links, or localhost profiling commands. No evidence found of malicious instructions, credential theft, or external data exfiltration. One semantic availability finding covers pipeline examples whose blocking receives can prevent cancellation and retain goroutines.

remediation.issue: Pipeline transformation and fan-in examples block on input receives without observing cancellation.
remediation.suggestion: Select between ctx.Done() and each input receive, handle channel closure, and test cancellation while inputs remain open and idle.

semantic_findings.title: Pipeline receives can ignore cancellation
semantic_findings.description: The square and fanIn examples range over input channels before checking cancellation. Open, idle inputs can retain workers after cancellation; repeated use can exhaust resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples check ctx.Done() only after receiving a value. Cancellation cannot unblock their input receives when channels remain open and idle.

content.value_statement: Concurrent Go code can hide goroutine leaks, shared-state races, and blocked pipelines. This skill guides implementation and review with lifecycle checklists and synchronization examples.
actual_capabilities: Guides goroutine ownership, shutdown, cancellation, and waiting decisions.
Explains channel direction, sender-owned closure, buffer sizing, and timer reuse.
Compares mutexes, atomics, sync.Map, sync.Pool, and one-time initialization.
Provides WaitGroup, errgroup, and singleflight examples with version-specific guidance.
Outlines bounded worker pools, fan-out, fan-in, and sequential iterator alternatives.
Organizes concurrency reviews across lifecycle, shared state, channels, timers, and synchronization.
limitations: Guidance cannot prove race freedom or replace tests against the actual application.
Some pipeline examples need cancellation-aware input receives before production use.
API availability and profiling instructions require verification against the project Go version.
General defensive coding and incident debugging are outside its primary scope.

use_cases.title: Build a bounded background worker
use_cases.description: Design worker ownership, concurrency limits, error propagation, and shutdown behavior before adding background tasks.

use_cases.title: Review concurrent pull requests
use_cases.description: Inspect changed goroutines, channel closure, shared state, and cancellation paths using a focused review checklist.

use_cases.title: Audit service concurrency
use_cases.description: Coordinate a codebase review across lifecycle management, synchronization, channel ownership, and resource bounds.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a synchronization primitive
prompt_templates.prompt: For this Go shared-state example, compare channels, mutexes, and atomics. Recommend the simplest option and explain ownership: [code].

prompt_templates.title: Review a concurrent change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go diff for goroutine leaks, unsafe channel closure, shared-state races, and missing cancellation. Explain each issue and propose focused fixes: [diff].

prompt_templates.title: Implement bounded concurrent work
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [task] in Go [version] with errgroup, a limit of [N], first-error cancellation, and ordered results. Include shutdown tests.

prompt_templates.title: Audit pipeline shutdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [scope] for channel ownership, blocked receives, cancellation, and concurrency bounds. Coordinate focused reviewers when available; prioritize findings and propose idle-input cancellation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: auditing concurrency across a codebase.

output_examples.input: Review a function that calls WaitGroup.Add inside each new goroutine.
output: Wait can return before goroutines register, leaving work running after the function returns.
Register work before launching goroutines and defer completion inside each worker.
For suitable Go 1.25+ tasks, consider WaitGroup.Go; use errgroup when error propagation or cancellation is required.

output_examples.input: Choose synchronization for a cache with frequent writes to overlapping keys.
output: Start with a plain map protected by a mutex or RWMutex.
sync.Map targets write-once/read-many or disjoint-key access patterns, so it is not the default choice here.
Keep critical sections short and benchmark the actual workload.

output_examples.input: Audit a fan-in function whose input channels may stay open after cancellation.
output: An unconditional channel receive cannot observe cancellation while the input is idle.
Select between cancellation and each receive, and handle closed channels explicitly.
Test cancellation with every input open and idle, then verify all workers and the output closer finish.

best_practices: Define each goroutine owner, stop signal, and waiting mechanism before implementation.
Test cancellation during blocked sends and receives, then run race and goroutine leak checks.
Match APIs to the project Go version and justify concurrency limits with workload measurements.
anti_patterns: Launching unbounded goroutines without shutdown or waiting mechanisms.
Closing producer channels from consumers or mutating shared data without synchronization.
Copying pipeline examples without testing cancellation when input channels remain open.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers goroutine lifecycle, channels, synchronization primitives, bounded concurrency, pipelines, and concurrency-focused code review.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The skill declares compatibility with Claude Code and Codex, or similar harnesses that support skill instructions.

faq.question: Does it require a Go installation?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Go as a prerequisite. Running tests and profiling commands requires an appropriate local Go toolchain.

faq.question: Does it automatically run a concurrency analyzer?
faq.answer: No bundled analyzer is included. The skill supplies instructions, reference examples, and evaluation prompts for the assistant.

faq.question: Are its examples ready for production?
faq.answer: Review them against your application and Go version. Some pipeline receives need cancellation handling, and all generated changes require testing.

faq.question: Can it diagnose an existing production hang?
faq.answer: Its primary focus is design and review. It references a separate troubleshooting skill for investigating specific hangs, crashes, and races.
